scope.population: one row per (counterparty, coin) with at least one finite score in each half of the day range
scope.window: features on days 4-8, label on days 9-13; the two halves are disjoint so no fill feeds both

declared_not_confirmed.note: settings.py declares these; this run did not state what it used, so they are the declaration and not a property of this artifact

label_definition: label_toxic_late = 1 when the counterparty's mean mo10_mid over the late half of the days is above zero. Cost-blind by construction: it counts wallets, not dollars, so a wallet doing one harmful fill and a wallet doing a thousand weigh the same. The continuous label in the column beside it is the economically meaningful target and is kept for that reason.
leakage_note: The day halves are disjoint, so no fill feeds both a feature and the label. That blocks label leakage and NOT counterparty leakage: a wallet appears in both halves by design, which is the whole point of the question, so any held-out evaluation must split on the wallet or on the coin.
why_this_window: Named from settings.headline_mid_col(), so the column names move with the declaration and cannot hold one window under another window's name. The frame this replaces carried the 60 s TRADE-PRINT markout under names ending mo60, which is a different quantity from the 10 s book mid this work reports on.
